title: [HiCache] Give trailing sidecar storage transfers a contiguous prefix_keys chain
body_opening:
## Motivation

`HiCacheStorageExtraInfo.prefix_keys` is the page-hash chain preceding a storage call's keys, from the sequence start. The KV path honors that: `_page_backup` and `_storage_hit_query` extend it batch by batch, so `prefix_keys + keys` is always one contiguous chain.

Trailing sidecar transfers (SWA window, Mamba state, and the pools derived from them) do not. Their keys are the last `N` pages of the node, but `prefix_keys` is still the node's ancestor chain, so the node's own pages before the window belong to neither:

```
KV     prefix=[h0]  keys=[h1 h2 h3 h4 h5 h6]   contiguous
SWA    prefix=[h0]  keys=[h5 h6]               h1..h4 missing
MAMBA  prefix=[h0]  keys=[h6]

body_opening:
## What this PR does
Hardcodes `BLOCK_SIZE=1024` in `count_expert_num_tokens` instead of computing it as `next_power_of_2(min(numel, 1024))`. The latter is a runtime-varying `tl.constexpr`, which forces a Triton kernel recompile every time `numel` crosses a new power-of-2 boundary — one of several instances flagged in #48650.

The kernel's existing masking logic (`tl.cdiv(topk_numel, BLOCK_SIZE)`-based loop with per-iteration masks) already handles any `BLOCK_SIZE` correctly regardless of the actual `numel`, so this is a pure performance fix with no behavior change.

title: [DSV4] perf: Make FP8 quant output tensor contiguous
body_opening:
## Motivation

This PR is an alternative way to achieve https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27680.

Deep gemm FP8 einsum silently falls back to an unoptimized path if the input tensor is not contiguous. We can make the `per_token_group_quant_8bit_v2` to emit the scale layout needed by deep gemm.

This also implicitly fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29038. The previous DSV4 `wo_a` FP8 DeepGEMM path flattened `o: [T, G, D]` into `[T * G, D]` and then viewed the scales back as `[T, G, -1]`.
